adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Reusing existing Redis SET keys for ZADD and ZSCAN causes WRONGTYPE failures after deployment, blocking ingestion and flushing until old buffers expire or are drained.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to SORTED SET operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in both buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The key format remains the same (e.g., 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:parent_span_id'). During deployment, existing keys created as SETs will still exist in Redis, but the new code will attempt SORTED SET operations on them. Redis returns WRONGTYPE errors when you try to use commands for one data type on keys of another type. This would cause failures until the old SET keys expire (based on set_timeout) or are manually cleared.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — Replaying a child batch after its parent resolves sums duplicate timestamps in ZUNIONSTORE, causing older spans to outrank newer spans during eviction.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate timestamps, but this is incorrect. Redis ZUNIONSTORE with default AGGREGATE SUM behavior would sum scores for identical members, but in this context each span payload is unique (different span data), so there are no duplicate members to sum. The spans being merged have different payloads, so their scores (timestamps) are preserved independently. The finding misunderstands how ZUNIONSTORE works with unique members.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — ZADD and ZSCAN reuse keys previously populated by SADD, so existing buffered segments cause WRONGTYPE failures during deployment until drained or migrated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (SADD, SSCAN, SCARD, SUNIONSTORE) to SORTED SET commands (ZADD, ZSCAN, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The keys follow the pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:span_id'. During deployment, existing data stored with SADD (as sets) will still exist in Redis, but the new code will try to use ZADD/ZSCAN on those same keys. Redis does not allow mixing data types on the same key - attempting ZADD on a key that contains a SET will result in a WRONGTYPE error. This is a real deployment/migration bug that will cause failures until existing buffered data is drained or explicitly migrated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — Replaying a child after its parent buffer merges sums its duplicate timestamp in ZUNIONSTORE, causing eviction to retain old spans ahead of newer spans.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE is used with 'AGGREGATE SUM' by default (line 53: `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`). When a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has already merged, the same span payload would be added again with its timestamp score. ZUNIONSTORE with SUM aggregation would add the scores together, doubling the timestamp value for duplicate spans. This corrupted score would affect the ZPOPMIN eviction logic (lines 61-63), potentially causing newer spans to be evicted instead of older ones since the duplicated span would have an artificially high score.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The new hard-coded 1000-span eviction cap bypasses the still-exposed `max_segment_spans` setting, leaving a misleading no-op configuration and two divergent limits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hard-coded limit of 1000 spans in the Lua script (line 62: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`). Looking at buffer.py, there is indeed a `max_segment_spans` configuration that was previously used (lines 443-449 show the removed code that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The finding correctly identifies that the Lua script now enforces a hard-coded 1000 limit while the Python configuration `max_segment_spans` still exists but is no longer effective for this enforcement. This is a legitimate architectural concern about divergent limits and potentially misleading configuration, though not a bug per se since the system will still function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a single-use subclass that copies nearly all of `BasePaginator.get_result`, so future cursor fixes must be kept in two implementations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912 in paginator.py) duplicates most of the get_result logic from BasePaginator. Looking at the diff, the new class copies the entire pagination algorithm including cursor handling, offset calculation, result slicing, and cursor building - with only minor modifications for 'enable_advanced_features'. This creates a maintenance burden where future bug fixes to cursor pagination logic would need to be applied in two places. This is a legitimate architectural/maintainability concern grounded in the actual code added by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without a migration makes `ZADD` fail with `WRONGTYPE` for up to the one-hour TTL during rollout, causing background ingestion batches to fail until old buffers expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis set operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted set operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) for the same keys (span-buf:s:*). In buffer.py line 197, the code changes from `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` to `p.zadd(set_key, ...)`. Similarly, the Lua script in add-buffer.lua changes from `scard`/`sunionstore` to `zcard`/`zunionstore`. Redis does not allow mixing set and sorted set operations on the same key - attempting ZADD on an existing set key returns WRONGTYPE error. During rollout, existing keys created with SADD will still exist (with TTL up to the timeout), and new code trying ZADD on those keys will fail. This is a real migration/compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — ZUNIONSTORE` uses Redis's default `SUM` aggregation, so an at-least-once retry of an already-buffered span inflates its timestamp score and can make the 1,000-span eviction discard newer legitimate spans instead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE being used at lines 47 and 52 in add-buffer.lua without specifying an aggregation method, which defaults to SUM in Redis. When the same span payload is processed multiple times (at-least-once delivery), its score (end_timestamp_precise) would be summed, artificially inflating it. Combined with the zpopmin eviction at line 61 that removes spans with the lowest scores, this could cause newer legitimate spans to be evicted instead of older ones, since the duplicated span would have an inflated score. This is a real correctness bug in the span buffering logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — No test inserts or merges more than 1,000 spans with distinct timestamps, so the new eviction branch's cap, boundary, and oldest-span ordering can regress without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new eviction logic in add-buffer.lua at lines 55-62 that caps spans at 1000 and uses zpopmin to remove oldest spans when exceeded. Looking at the test files in the diff (test_buffer.py, test_flusher.py, test_consumer.py), none of the test cases insert more than a handful of spans (typically 4-5 spans per test). The finding correctly identifies that this new eviction branch with the 1000 span cap, boundary conditions, and oldest-span ordering via zpopmin is not covered by any test in the diff. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic.
